entities.summary: Uruguay is a sovereign nation in South America, Americas. Its capital is Montevideo. Official languages include Spanish. Government: Unitary presidential constitutional republic. Population: approximately 3.4 million. Area: 176,215 km². Comprehensive index for Uruguay covering Charra indigenous peoples (fiercely resisted Spanish, near extinction), Spanish colonization (Montevideo founded 1724), Banda Oriental (disputed between Spain/Portugal/Argentina/Brazil), José Artigas (national hero, federalist, Liga Federal, exile Paraguay), Brazilian occupation 1817-28, independence 1828 (buffer state), Blancos vs Colorados civil wars, Battle of the Plates 1843-51 (Great Siege Montevideo), European immigration waves (Italian/Spanish, 1870-1930, ~40% population replaced), José Batlle y Ordóñez progressive reforms (early 20th century welfare state), Switzerland of South America, Tupamaros (MLN-T, urban guerrillas 1960s-70s, Mujica), military dictatorship 1973-85 (Operation Condor, human rights abuses), return to democracy, marijuana legalization 2013 (first country), and smallest Hispanic country.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Uruguay's struggle for independence and its subsequent civil wars had significant regional impact, shaping the politics of South America. The country's unique history as a buffer state between European powers also influenced its development.
